item.title: A $\mathbb{C}$-motivic $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1
item.description: arXiv:2610.22651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathrm{DY} = \mathbb{1}/(\eta, \nu) \in \mathrm{SH}(\mathbb{C})$. We construct a $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1 $w:\Sigma^{5,3}\mathrm{DY} \to \mathrm{DY}.$ The cofiber is a realization of $DA(1)$, the double of the subalgebra $A(1)$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Steenrod algebra $A$.
item.dc:creator: Jackson Morris

item.title: Rational torus equivariant spectra VII: the Cousin complex
item.description: arXiv:2610.23164v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the analogy between rational G-spectra for an r-torus G and sheaves over an r-dimensional scheme, in the context of the author's algebraic model for rational G-spectra. In particular, the resolution of the sphere of a virtual representation in the standard model corresponds precisely to the Cousin complex resolution of a line bundle. The tom Dieck splitting for the sphere of an actual respresentation corresponds to the collapse of the Cousin spectral sequence by degrees, and the the non collapse in other cases corresponds to familiar geometric behaviour.
item.dc:creator: J. P. C. Greenlees

item.title: The Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for p >= 11
item.description: arXiv:2610.23215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for all primes p >= 11. This improves on the recently announced result by OpenAI that V(4) exists at the prime 1009.
item.dc:creator: Vigleik Angeltveit

item.title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face. Moreover, the supports form a simplicial subset of the event space. This naturally raises the question of how the topology of this simplicial subset is related to the corresponding carrier face. Our main objective is to relate the dimension of the carrier face to the topology and combinatorial structure of the space of supports. For $n$-facet-paired measurement spaces, we first express the carrier dimension in terms of the nullity of an associated facet matrix. When the measurement space is additionally orientable, we show that the carrier dimension is determined by the top-dimensional homology of the space of supports, yielding, in particular, a homological criterion for detecting vertices. We then develop an algebraic reduction based on a strong connectivity relation on the generating simplices of the space of supports. This construction yields a reduced facet matrix, indexed by the strongly connected components, whose null space is isomorphic to that of the original facet matrix. As a consequence, both the carrier dimension and extremality can be determined from the topology of the support and the way its strongly connected components are glued together.
item.dc:creator: Aziz Kharoof, Chung-Ping Lai

item.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Brunialti

item.title: Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map
item.description: arXiv:2610.23758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define. This allows us to extend the definition of Brugall\'e and Wickelgren's quadratically enriched binomial coefficients to arbitrary Grothendieck--Witt classes. This allows for a new proof that quadratically enriched binomial coefficients depend only on the trace form of the inputted \'etale algebra, as well as an elegant reproof of a result of Chen and Wickelgren about binomial coefficients over finite fields.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Brazelton, Ben Spitz

item.title: A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.23838v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.
item.dc:creator: Marco Delgado-Garrido, Lars Moberg Salbu, Alvaro Torras-Casas, Rocio Gonzalez-Diaz

item.title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.23855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(\chi(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.
item.dc:creator: Zhi L\"u, Jun Ma, Qiangbo Tan

item.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $\kappa$ for which they are $\kappa$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.
item.dc:creator: Wern Juin Gabriel Ong, Gabriel Ribeiro

item.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.
item.dc:creator: Jean Fasel, Maria Yakerson

item.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.
item.dc:creator: Taito Shimoji

item.title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.23637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Bartholdi, Martin R. Bridson, Roman Mikhailov, John Nicholson

item.title: Extra-fine sheaves and interaction decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2009.12646v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce an original notion of (upper) extra-fine sheaf on a topological space, for which \v{C}ech cohomology in strictly positive degree vanishes. We apply this notion when the topological space is a partially ordered set (poset) equipped with the Alexandroff topology and the sheaves are made of duals of decomposable functors of vector spaces. The decomposition of the functor is known as interaction decomposition and can be expressed by a novel sum-intersection condition. We use these results to compute the dimension of the space of global sections when the sheaves are derived from those freely generated over a presheaf (of finite sets); this generalizes and makes topological classical counting formulae for the number of solutions of the linearized marginal problem (Kellerer and Mat\'u\v{s}). We finish with a comparison theorem between the \v{C}ech cohomology associated to a covering and the topos cohomology of the poset with coefficients in the presheaf, which is also the cohomology of a cosimplicial local system over the nerve of the poset. For that, we give a detailed treatment of cosimplicial local systems on simplicial sets. The appendixes present presheaves, sheaves relative \v{C}ech cohomology, and their application to the marginal problem.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Bennequin, Olivier Peltre, Gr\'egoire Sergeant-Perthuis, Juan Pablo Vigneaux

item.title: A Poincar\'e-Lefschetz Theorem for Cellular Cosheaves and an Application to the Tropical Homology of Orbifold Toric Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2308.08548v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We begin by presenting a version of the Poincar\'e-Lefschetz theorem for certain cellular cosheaves on a particular subdivision of a CW-complex K. To that end we construct a cellular sheaf on K whose cohomology with compact support is isomorphic to the homology of the initial cosheaf. Thereafter we use the first result to generalise the tropical version of the Lefschetz Hyperplane Section Theorem to some singular tropical toric varieties and singular tropical hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jules Chenal

item.title: Parametrised functor calculus: excision, spheres, and semiadditivity
item.description: arXiv:2410.22327v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We lay down the foundations of a theory of parametrised functor calculus, generalising parts of the functor calculus of Goodwillie. We introduce the notion of excisable posets and develop a theory of excisive approximations in this context. As an application, we introduce two different excisable posets when parametrising over an atomic orbital category. By comparing the notions of excisiveness for these two posets, we relate the invertibility of certain spheres with Nardin's notion of parametrised semiadditivity, generalising Wirthm\"uller's classical result in equivariant homotopy theory for finite groups.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: J. Lond. Math. Soc. (2026) Vol. 114, Issue 4
item.dc:creator: Kaif Hilman, Sil Linskens

item.title: Continuous Comparison of Free Simplicial Prounipotent and Pro-$p$ Resolutions
item.description: arXiv:2609.21513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a continuous version of the comparison theorem for free simplicial resolutions in the categories of prounipotent groups over a field of characteristic zero and of pro-$p$ groups. The resolutions carry free bases compatible with degeneracies; their ranks may be infinite. In characteristic zero the lifting step follows from continuous linear splittings and the universal property of completed free Lie algebras. In the pro-$p$ case it follows from the classical projectivity of free pro-$p$ groups. A relative lifting argument and an explicit simplicial cylinder establish homotopy uniqueness. We formulate the free bases using actual surjections in the simplex category, so degeneracy words related by simplicial identities are identified from the outset, and we spell out the full matching objects used in the lifting argument. The question arose naturally in our preceding work on Bousfield--Kan completions of subcontractible presentations.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Mikhovich

item.title: Bousfield--Kan Completions of Subcontractible Presentations
item.description: arXiv:2609.21534v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Bousfield--Kan completions through the interaction of free simplicial resolutions, their filtration spectral sequences, and a noncommutative arithmetic square. For every free discrete simplicial group of finite type, we express its integral pronilpotent completion as the homotopy pullback of its rational prounipotent completion and the product of its pro-$p$ completions over an explicit adelic simplicial group. The adelic entry is formed by taking restricted products at finite nilpotent stages and then their inverse limit; no nilpotency assumption on the original group of components is required. Finite subpresentations of contractible presentations provide an explicit application of this construction. Independence of the specified relators makes the positive-degree terms of the rational and mod-$p$ filtration spectral sequences vanish, with convergence verified on the quotient towers. Continuous comparison of free simplicial resolutions then realizes, in characteristic zero, the equivalence with a constant free prounipotent group by morphisms and homotopies in that category. For the corresponding presentation complex $K$ we obtain $R_\infty K\simeq K(F_R(Z),1)$ for $R=\mathbb Q,\mathbb F_p,\mathbb Z$, where $Z$ indexes a complementary basis and $F_R(Z)$ denotes, respectively, the rational points of a free prounipotent group, a free pro-$p$ group, or a free pronilpotent group. Compatible contractions at the nilpotent stages identify all four entries of the arithmetic square in this case.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Mikhovich

item.title: Equivariant Chow functions and Wonderful Models in type A and B
item.description: arXiv:2610.03138v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a general inversion formula in the equivariant incidence algebras of geometric lattices that relates the equivariant Chow function with the equivariant super-reduced characteristic function. We apply this result to the case of minimal wonderful models for hyperplane arrangements associated to root systems, with the natural action of the corresponding Weyl group. Applying this formula to type $A$ (i.e. the partition lattices), we recover Getzler's compositional identity in type $A$. In type $B$ (i.e. the signed partition lattice), we recover Henderson's result, expressing the equivariant Chow generating series in terms of the same series in type $A$ and the equivariant characteristic generating series of type $B$. Moreover, we obtain a new compositional identity for the equivariant Chow generating series.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Pagaria, Tommaso Scognamiglio

item.title: Non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery
item.description: arXiv:2610.21100v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give homotopy-theoretic proofs of the principal results of non-simply connected Poincar\'e surgery. These include the Fundamental Theorem of Poincar\'e surgery, the Poincar\'e transversality exact sequence, and the construction of Poincar\'e handle structures. All results apply in dimensions~$\ge 8$.
item.dc:creator: John R. Klein

item.title: On the torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of smooth quasi-projective varieties of rank up to seven
item.description: arXiv:2510.09026v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective variety. Assume that the (topological) fundamental group $\pi_1(X, x)$ is torsion-free nilpotent. We show that if the first Betti number $b_1(X) \le 3$, then $\pi_1(X, x)$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for $n = 1, 2, 3$, a lattice in the Heisenberg group $H_3(\mathbb{R})$ or $\mathbb{R} \times H_3(\mathbb{R})$. Moreover, we prove that $\pi_1(X, x)$ is abelian or $2$-step nilpotent if its rank is less than or equal to seven. More precisely, we determine the real nilpotent Lie groups in which torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups can be embedded as lattices for ranks up to six and seven, respectively. Our main results are a partial positive answer to a question on nilpotent (quasi-)K\"ahler groups posed by Aguilar and Campana.
item.dc:creator: Taito Shimoji

item.title: Equivariant localizing motives and multiplicative norms on algebraic K-theory
item.description: arXiv:2603.15873v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct multiplicative norms on equivariant nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory for finite groups $G$. We also construct a genuine equivariant version of THH equipped with a Dennis trace map from K-theory compatible with the multiplicative norms. To do so, we follow the general strategy of Blumberg-Gepner-Tabuada in the nonequivariant case by generalizing their category of localizing motives to the genuine equivariant context, building upon the theory of perfect $G$-stable categories of the first-named author. Crucially, we proceed using the recent perspective on noncommutative motives by the second-named author with Sosnilo and Winges which allows us to deal with non-exact functors on this category of motives. Together with an isotropy separation argument for equivariant cubes, we prove our main theorem that norms of stable categories preserve equivariant motivic equivalences. As an immediate consequence, we obtain a unique equivariant multiplicative refinement of nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory. From these constructions and results, we draw several applications, namely: (1) that the endofunctor of (equivariant) tensor powers on ordinary perfect stable categories preserve motivic equivalences; (2) that the multiplicative norms also preserve the additive motivic equivalences, thus yielding a motivic refinement of a result of Elmanto-Haugseng and Cnossen-Haugseng-Lenz-Linskens that connective algebraic K-theory admits multiplicative norms; (3) we construct a genuine equivariant version of topological Hochschild homology equipped with a Dennis trace map that is compatible with multiplicative norms; and (4) we prove that every genuine $G$-spectrum is the K-theory of a perfect $G$-stable category.
item.dc:creator: Kaif Hilman, Maxime Ramzi
